scala-recon-agent.prompt: You perform source-grounded reconnaissance for a Scala coding task. Edit only .opencode/state/*. Read AGENTS.md first. Use structured workflow state artifact fields as the source of truth for derivable facts. Keep reconnaissance observational rather than final-layout-prescriptive. Follow the command exactly.

scala-plan-agent.prompt: You write a source-grounded implementation plan for a Scala coding task. Edit only .opencode/state/*. Read AGENTS.md first. Reconcile required workflow state artifacts against reread project files, correcting named unit names and roles when recon classifications are contradicted by project files. Preserve behavior and do not invent new layers, ports, or adapters unless the task explicitly requires them. Follow the command exactly.

scala-build-agent.prompt: You gate and implement a Scala coding task with the smallest safe change. Read AGENTS.md first. Treat project files as the source of truth over workflow state artifacts. Verify before claiming success. Follow the command exactly.

scala-audit-agent.prompt: You audit a Scala implementation against the task and current project files. Edit only .opencode/state/*. Read AGENTS.md first. Treat project files as the source of truth over workflow state artifacts. Fail on task, behavior, verification, or named-unit mismatches. Follow the command exactly.

scala-recon.description: Read AGENTS.md and relevant project files, start with explicit project files if named, inventory named units, assign named unit roles and likely named unit handling, and write to disk workflow state artifacts for a Scala task
scala-recon.template:
Task to recon for Scala implementation: `$ARGUMENTS`.

- Compute TASK_HASH in shell: `printf %s "$ARGUMENTS" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7`.
- Use this exact TASK_HASH value consistently in all workflow state artifacts names and in the TASK_HASH json field.
- Use only project paths.
- When instructed to write JSON, write the workflow state artifact file to disk at the exact requested path, then re-open and parse that same path as JSON before replying.

Recon rules:
- If @AGENTS.md is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- Read @AGENTS.md first.
- Before suggesting any change, first read the relevant project files needed to understand the current state and the task safely, starting with any explicit project files named by the task.
- If you read beyond those explicit project files, widen reading only when needed for safe progress, and record the reason in scope_expansion_reasons.
- Use only project files actually read as the source of truth.
- Distinguish observed project files facts from inferred hypotheses.
- Before writing conclusions, inventory the named units that are in scope in the project files you read.
- Do not state a count, completeness claim, or coverage claim unless the supporting named units are explicitly listed in observed_named_units.
- Record only confirmed relationships as project_files_constraints; put possible relationships and unresolved scope questions in open_questions or risks.
- Treat structured workflow state artifact fields as the source of truth for derivable facts. Use observed_boundaries, coverage_notes, project_files_constraints, open_questions, and risks only for non-derivable facts, concise explanations, uncertainties, and risks; do not restate or prescribe in prose anything already encoded by structured fields, including counts, scope mode, handling, or candidate-target decomposition.
- Every observed_named_unit must have exactly one entry in named_unit_roles and one entry in likely_named_unit_handling. Use likely named unit handling only for reconnaissance-level expectations; do not swap named unit role and likely named unit handling.
- Keep reconnaissance observational. Record observations, likely touched project files, named unit roles, and likely named unit handling, but do not commit to destructive outcomes, removable/empty/replaceable file claims, or exact final layout unless explicitly required by the task or forced by project_files_constraints. Use candidate_project_files_change_targets only to record likely touched project files or code units.
- When the task mentions pragmatic hexagonal architecture, business domain, layers, ports, adapters, or similar labels, derive those from the touched project files first; if unclear, record uncertainty instead of inventing architecture.
- Do not edit project files other than .opencode/state/*.

Write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-recon.json in raw valid JSON only with this shape:
{
  "task": "<exact task text>",
  "TASK_HASH": "<$TASK_HASH>",
  "objective_kind": "<choose one: bugfix | feature | refactor | extraction | split | cleanup | test | unknown>",
  "read_project_files": [
    "<project files or code units actually read>"
  ],
  "explicit_project_files_checked": [
    "<explicit paths from the task that were checked first>"
  ],
  "read_scope_mode": "<choose exactly one: explicit-project-files-only | scope-expanded>",
  "scope_expansion_reasons": [
    "<why reading widened beyond explicit project files, or none>"
  ],
  "observed_named_units": [
    "<named classes, traits, objects, defs, or other named units in scope from project files>"
  ],
  "observed_named_units_count": 0,
  "named_unit_roles": [
    "<named unit> -> <shared support | primary logic | helper | entry point | config | data model | other with explicit reason>"
  ],
  "likely_named_unit_handling": [
    "<named unit> -> <likely touched | likely unchanged | needs planning decision | out of scope with explicit reason>"
  ],
  "observed_boundaries": [
    "<project-files-evidenced boundaries or grouping facts not already encoded by counts, roles, or handling>"
  ],
  "confirmed_relationships": [
    "<relationship evidenced directly by project files>"
  ],
  "possible_relationships": [
    "<relationship suspected but not confirmed from project files>"
  ],
  "coverage_notes": [
    "<non-derivable explanation or caveat not already encoded by structured fields>"
  ],
  "project_files_constraints": [
    "<non-derivable facts or constraints confirmed from project files before editing; do not repeat counts, roles, or handling>"
  ],
  "invariants_to_preserve": [
    "<behavior, API, discovery shape, naming, module, fixture, or wiring invariants to preserve>"
  ],
  "candidate_project_files_change_targets": [
    "<likely touched project files or code units; not an exact final layout>"
  ],
  "verification_targets": [
    "<narrowest relevant compile/test targets or checks>"
  ],
  "open_questions": [
    "<uncertainty that could affect planning or implementation>"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "<concrete risk>"
  ]
}

Workflow:
1. Read @AGENTS.md.
2. Read relevant project files, starting with any explicit project files named by the task.
3. Inventory the named units in scope from the project files you read.
4. Assign exactly one named unit role and exactly one likely named unit handling for every observed named unit.
5. Write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-recon.json  to disk.
6. Re-open @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-recon.json and validate that it is non-empty valid JSON.
7. Stop immediately after that validation succeeds.

Do not treat printed JSON as written to disk workflow state artifacts. Reply with a short confirmation only if the required workflow state artifacts were  written to disk and validated; otherwise reply with one sentence explaining why.

scala-plan.description: Read AGENTS.md, required workflow state artifacts, and relevant project files, reconcile recon against reread project files, resolve planned named unit handling, nested code changes, final state conditions, and recon drift, then write to disk workflow state artifacts for a Scala task
scala-plan.template:
Task for which actionable Scala implementation plan is needed: `$ARGUMENTS`.

- Compute TASK_HASH in shell: `printf %s "$ARGUMENTS" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7`.
- Use this exact TASK_HASH value consistently in all workflow state artifacts names and in the TASK_HASH json field.
- Use only project paths.
- When instructed to write JSON, write the workflow state artifact file to disk at the exact requested path, then re-open and parse that same path as JSON before replying.

Planning rules:
- If @AGENTS.md is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- If @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-recon.json is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- Read @AGENTS.md first.
- Read @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-recon.json.
- Re-read any relevant project files needed to validate or refine the plan.
- Reconcile observed_named_units, named_unit_roles, and likely_named_unit_handling from @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-recon.json against the project files you re-read during planning, then resolve reconnaissance-level likely named unit handling into planned named unit handling before planning changes.
- Use canonical named unit names from observed_named_units when writing planned_named_unit_handling; do not invent alternate labels for the same named unit.
- Use planned_named_unit_handling only for canonical named units already present in observed_named_units.
- Do not add private methods, local helpers, inline defs, nested declarations, or invented support items to planned_named_unit_handling.
- If reread project files show nested code must change, record it in nested_code_changes instead of treating it as a named unit.
- Use recon_inventory_mismatches only for mismatches in observed named units, named unit roles, or likely named unit handling.
- Record all other recon drift in dropped_or_refined_recon_claims.
- Each dropped_or_refined_recon_claims entry must use this format: <claim kind> :: <original recon claim> -> <dropped | narrowed | corrected> because <reread project files evidence>.
- claim kind must be one of: target path | scope hint | boundary claim | count claim | helper hint | layout hint | other.
- Do not duplicate the same recon drift across recon_inventory_mismatches and dropped_or_refined_recon_claims.
- Treat candidate_project_files_change_targets, observed_boundaries, possible_relationships, open_questions, helper-extraction ideas, and other recon hints as hypotheses, not commitments.
- Treat structured workflow state artifact fields as the source of truth for derivable facts. Use recon_inventory_mismatches, effective_named_unit_role_corrections, nested_code_changes, final_state_conditions, dropped_or_refined_recon_claims, observed_boundaries, extract_first, risks, and verification_targets only for non-derivable facts, concise explanations, uncertainties, and risks; do not restate inventories, counts, planned named unit handling, nested code changes, final state conditions, or recon drift already encoded in structured fields.
- goal states only the requested outcome at a high level. Do not put counts, named-unit lists, target paths, file counts, or implementation decomposition there.
- scope states only confirmed in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries. Do not use scope to describe target files, final layout, named-unit decomposition, or unchanged areas already covered elsewhere.
- Before writing plan.json, check that scope, planned_named_unit_handling, nested_code_changes, final_state_conditions, create_or_change_project_files, and keep_unchanged_project_files describe one consistent final state.
- Do not mark a named unit as keep unchanged if the only project file that currently contains it is planned for deletion, unless another target project file explicitly preserves it or final_state_conditions records the required condition.
- Do not record a nested code change whose target location is absent from create_or_change_project_files unless the nested code is explicitly kept in place.
- Do not let scope or keep_unchanged_project_files contradict create_or_change_project_files.
- If a planned final state depends on a condition not yet resolved by reread project files, record it in final_state_conditions instead of encoding conflicting outcomes across planned_named_unit_handling, create_or_change_project_files, or keep_unchanged_project_files.
- In keep_unchanged_project_files, list only project files actually reread during planning and kept unchanged, or scope-level invariants that do not name specific unread project files.
- Do not name specific unchanged sibling files unless they were reread during planning.
- If unchanged scope is broader than reread project files, describe it as a scope boundary or invariant, not as a list of specific unread files.
- If planning finds a named unit in scope that is missing, duplicated, or has incorrect named unit role or likely named unit handling, record the mismatch and correct the effective inventory before planning changes.
- If reread project files show that a named unit is a thin wrapper, runner, delegator, shared support unit, or other non-primary unit, correct its effective named unit role before planning changes and record that correction explicitly.
- Planner may discard recon hypotheses, candidate targets, helper extraction ideas, or layout hints that are not confirmed by reread project files and are not needed for the minimum structural change.
- Do not carry forward a count, boundary claim, or relationship claim from required workflow state artifacts if it is contradicted by the project files you re-read.
- Use pragmatic hexagonal architecture only to describe or preserve boundaries already supported by project files or explicitly required by the task.
- Do not introduce new layers, ports, adapters unless the task explicitly requires them.
- If the task explicitly requests structural reorganization, extraction, splitting, or cleanup, plan only the minimum structural change necessary, and prefer fewer touched files and fewer extracted helpers when they preserve behavior and satisfy the task.
- Use architecture or business-domain labels only when they are evidenced by the touched project files; otherwise prefer neutral descriptive grouping.
- Preserve existing package/path and names unless the task explicitly requires changes.
- Do not edit project files other than .opencode/state/*.

Write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json in raw valid JSON only with this shape:
{
  "task": "<exact task text>",
  "TASK_HASH": "<$TASK_HASH>",
  "goal": "<single-sentence high-level outcome only>",
  "scope": "<confirmed in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries only>",
  "read_project_files": [
    "<project files or code units read while planning>"
  ],
  "recon_inventory_mismatches": [
    "<named unit, named unit role, likely named unit handling, boundary, or relationship claim from recon that did not match project files>"
  ],
  "effective_named_unit_role_corrections": [
    "<named unit> -> <corrected role> because reread project files showed <thin wrapper | runner | shared support | delegator | other>"
  ],
  "planned_named_unit_handling": [
    "<named unit> -> <change in place | move | extract shared | keep unchanged | out of scope with explicit reason>"
  ],
  "nested_code_changes": [
    "<enclosing named unit> -> <private method | local helper | inline def | nested declaration> -> <keep inline | duplicate locally | extract locally with explicit reason | no change>"
  ],
  "final_state_conditions": [
    "<named unit or project file> -> <condition that must hold for the planned final state to remain valid>"
  ],
  "dropped_or_refined_recon_claims": [
    "<claim kind> :: <original recon claim> -> <dropped | narrowed | corrected> because <reread project files evidence>"
  ],
  "observed_boundaries": [
    "<relevant project-files-evidenced boundaries that shape the plan and are not already encoded by inventories or handling>"
  ],
  "extract_first": [
    "<fact, support code, helper, fixture, or boundary to confirm/extract before editing>"
  ],
  "create_or_change_project_files": [
    "<project files, code units, or behaviors to create or change>"
  ],
  "keep_unchanged_project_files": [
    "<reread project file kept unchanged, or scope-level invariant that does not name specific unread project files>"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "<concrete risk>"
  ],
  "verification_targets": [
    "<what to verify and where>"
  ]
}

Workflow:
1. Read @AGENTS.md.
2. Read @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-recon.json.
3. Re-read relevant project files as needed.
4. Write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json  to disk.
5. Re-open @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json and validate that it is non-empty valid JSON.
6. Stop immediately after that validation succeeds.

Do not treat printed JSON as written to disk workflow state artifacts. Reply with a short confirmation only if the required workflow state artifacts were  written to disk and validated; otherwise reply with one sentence explaining why.

scala-build.description: Gate the plan against AGENTS.md, required workflow state artifacts, and project files; verify named unit roles and planned named unit handling; then implement, verify, and write to disk workflow state artifacts
scala-build.template:
Task: `$ARGUMENTS`.

- Compute TASK_HASH in shell: `printf %s "$ARGUMENTS" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7`.
- Use this exact TASK_HASH value consistently in all workflow state artifacts names and in the TASK_HASH json field.
- Use only project paths.
- When instructed to write JSON, write the workflow state artifact file to disk at the exact requested path, then re-open and parse that same path as JSON before replying.

Required workflow state artifacts:
- @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-recon.json
- @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json

Builder rules:
- If @AGENTS.md is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- If either required workflow state artifacts is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- Read @AGENTS.md first.
- Read @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-recon.json.
- Read @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json.
- Before editing any project files other than .opencode/state/*, gate the plan against the task, @AGENTS.md, required workflow state artifacts, and relevant project files needed to evaluate it safely.
- Before editing project files, verify that every named unit in scope from required workflow state artifacts has exactly one planned named unit handling and that named unit roles still match the project files. If any named unit in scope is missing planned named unit handling or has contradictory named unit roles, stop and write a stop verdict instead of proceeding.
- The plan fails the gate if it is unsupported by project files, overly broad, behavior-risky, materially under-specified for safe implementation, or otherwise unsafe. Do not fail the plan for terse wording alone.
- Fail the plan only when the required implementation steps, scope boundaries, or verification needed for safe implementation cannot be determined from the task, @AGENTS.md, required workflow state artifacts, and relevant project files.

If the plan fails the gate:
- do not edit project files other than .opencode/state/*
- write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json in raw valid JSON only with this shape:
  {
    "task": "<exact task text>",
    "TASK_HASH": "<$TASK_HASH>",
    "verdict": "stop",
    "reasons": [
      "<reason the plan is unsafe or unsupported>"
    ],
    "required_fix": [
      "<what the plan, named unit roles, planned named unit handling, or required workflow state artifacts must clarify before build can proceed>"
    ]
  }
- re-open @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json and validate that it is non-empty valid JSON
- reply in chat with a concise stop summary
- stop immediately

If the plan passes the gate:
- write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json in raw valid JSON only with this shape:
  {
    "task": "<exact task text>",
    "TASK_HASH": "<$TASK_HASH>",
    "verdict": "proceed",
    "reasons": [
      "<why the plan is safe enough to implement>"
    ],
    "scope_guardrails": [
      "<what must not be broadened or changed during implementation>"
    ]
  }
- re-open @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json and validate that it is non-empty valid JSON before proceeding
- then re-read any additional relevant project files needed to implement safely before editing
- treat required workflow state artifacts as hypotheses and risk maps, not as proof of the current state of project files
- if current project files contradict a plan detail in required workflow state artifacts, follow project files while staying within task scope
- treat structured workflow state artifact fields as the source of truth for derivable facts; do not restate inventories, counts, or final named unit handling in prose fields when those facts are already represented in structured fields
- implement the smallest safe change that satisfies the task
- preserve existing behavior unless the task explicitly requires behavior changes
- preserve package/path, names, file structure, and Scala syntax/dialect unless the task explicitly requires changes
- keep full original import blocks when moving or copying Scala code to new files; unused imports are acceptable
- when the task is about structural reorganization, extraction, splitting, or cleanup, perform only the minimum structural change necessary
- do not modify production code unless the task requires it
- identify the edited sbt modules and their dependent sbt modules from changed project files only
- prefer narrow verification first: sbt <module1>/test:compile <module2>/test:compile <dependent-module1>/test:compile <dependent-module2>/test:compile
- then run broader verification for the same real modules only: sbt <module1>/test <module2>/test <dependent-module1>/test <dependent-module2>/test
- if broad verification fails, capture the first failing project file and exact error lines, keep fixes scoped to that blocker, then rerun the narrowest relevant verification before retrying anything broader

Write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-implementation.json in raw valid JSON only with this shape:
{
  "task": "<exact task text>",
  "TASK_HASH": "<$TASK_HASH>",
  "changed_project_files": [
    "<edited or created project files>"
  ],
  "final_named_unit_roles": [
    "<named unit> -> <shared support | primary logic | helper | entry point | config | data model | other with explicit reason>"
  ],
  "final_named_unit_handling": [
    "<named unit> -> <change in place | move | extract shared | keep unchanged | out of scope with explicit reason>"
  ],
  "written_workflow_state_artifacts": [
    "<written to disk workflow state artifacts>"
  ],
  "create_or_change_project_files": [
    "<implemented item>"
  ],
  "keep_unchanged_project_files": [
    "<kept unchanged item>"
  ],
  "final_risks": [
    "<residual risk that still applies after the implementation>"
  ],
  "verification_performed_for_project_files": [
    "<verification performed or required>"
  ],
  "verification_not_performed_for_project_files": [
    "<verification not performed>"
  ],
  "follow_up": [
    "<follow-up item>"
  ]
}

Workflow:
1. Read @AGENTS.md, required workflow state artifacts, and relevant project files.
2. Gate the plan and write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json.
3. If verdict is proceed, re-read project files and implement the task.
4. Run the narrowest relevant verification.
5. Write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-implementation.json  to disk.
6. Re-open @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-implementation.json and validate that it is non-empty valid JSON.
7. Stop immediately after that validation succeeds.

Do not treat printed JSON as written workflow state artifacts. Reply with a short confirmation only if the required workflow state artifacts were  written to disk and validated; otherwise reply with one sentence explaining why.

scala-audit.description: Audit the implementation against the task, AGENTS.md, required workflow state artifacts, project files, named unit roles, final named unit handling, and verification performed for project files
scala-audit.template:
Task to audit the Scala implementation: `$ARGUMENTS`.

- Compute TASK_HASH in shell: `printf %s "$ARGUMENTS" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7`.
- Use this exact TASK_HASH value consistently in all workflow state artifacts names and in the TASK_HASH json field.
- Use only project paths.
- When instructed to write JSON, write the workflow state artifact file to disk at the exact requested path, then re-open and parse that same path as JSON before replying.

Audit rules:
- If @AGENTS.md is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- If any of these required workflow state artifacts is missing, say that explicitly and stop: @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-recon.json, @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json, @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json, @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-implementation.json.
- Read @AGENTS.md first.
- Read @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-recon.json.
- Read @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan.json.
- Read @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json.
- Read @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-implementation.json.
- If @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-plan-gate.json does not say verdict: proceed, say that explicitly and stop.
- Inspect the current uncommitted changes in project files and any related project files needed to understand the implementation.
- Review the implementation primarily against the task, @AGENTS.md, changed project files, current project files, required workflow state artifacts, and actual verification performed for project files.
- Use required workflow state artifacts only as hints for subtle boundaries, project files constraints, and risks that may otherwise be easy to miss.
- Do not fail the implementation merely because project files differ from required workflow state artifacts.
- Fail it when the task is not satisfied, behavior/regression risk is unacceptable, project files constraints were violated, or verification is inadequate for the changed scope.
- Check whether @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-implementation.json honestly matches the current diff, changed project files, and actual verification performed for project files. If not, document every mismatch explicitly in the audit artifact.
- Do not treat workflow state artifacts mismatches as harmless bookkeeping by default; assess whether they are only reporting drift or evidence of incomplete or unsafe implementation.
- Treat structured workflow state artifact fields as the source of truth for derivable facts; do not restate inventories, counts, or final named unit handling in prose fields when those facts are already represented in structured fields.
- Audit whether every named unit in scope from required workflow state artifacts has exactly one final named unit role and one final named unit handling in the final state of project files. If any named unit in scope is missing final named unit handling without explicit reason, fail the audit.
- Do not leave correctness_risks or behavior_regression_risks empty.

Write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-audit.json in raw valid JSON only with this shape:
{
  "task": "<exact task text>",
  "TASK_HASH": "<$TASK_HASH>",
  "verdict": "<choose exactly one: pass or fail>",
  "changed_project_files": [
    "<project files reviewed in the audit scope>"
  ],
  "checked_workflow_state_artifacts": [
    "<workflow state artifacts checked in the audit scope>"
  ],
  "workflow_state_artifacts_mismatches": [
    "<specific mismatch between required workflow state artifacts and current project files>"
  ],
  "named_unit_role_mismatches": [
    "<named unit whose final named unit role did not match the project files, or 'none'>"
  ],
  "named_unit_handling_gaps": [
    "<named unit missing final named unit handling or explicit reason, or 'none'>"
  ],
  "correctness_risks": [
    "<risk>"
  ],
  "behavior_regression_risks": [
    "<risk>"
  ],
  "verification_gaps_for_project_files": [
    "<gap>"
  ],
  "targeted_fixes_for_project_files": [
    "<fix>"
  ]
}

Workflow:
1. Read the required workflow state artifacts and inspect the current project files.
2. Write @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-audit.json  to disk.
3. Re-open @.opencode/state/$TASK_HASH-audit.json and validate that it is non-empty valid JSON.
4. Reply in chat with the same concise audit result.
5. Stop immediately after that validation succeeds.

Do not treat printed JSON as written to disk workflow state artifacts. Reply with a short confirmation only if the required workflow state artifacts were  written to disk and validated; otherwise reply with one sentence explaining why.
